history.summary: 9th-century Shiva temple on an island at the junction of the Pairi and Mahanadi rivers at the Triveni Sangam, Rajim - not the oldest temple in Rajim proper, but the oldest on the island. It stands on a 17-foot octagonal jagati, high enough to protect the shrine from Mahanadi floods, with steps for pilgrims arriving by boat; it is said to have stood on the mainland before a change in the river's course made it an island. The complex has two adjacent garbha-grhas sharing one mandapa - one sanctum holds the Kuleshvara linga, the other a Jagadamba shrine - with near life-size sculptures of Yamuna, Ganga, Kartikeya, Sitala Mata and Mahishasuramardini on the mandapa pilasters. Inscriptions of the Nala and Kalachuri periods are found here, and a partly damaged inscription dates the temple to the ninth century. It has been renovated, and a pedestrian bridge was completed in the late 2010s connecting it to Rajim. During monsoon floods it can become unapproachable. Not to be confused with similarly named temples in Kathmandu and elsewhere. District note: Rajim is officially in Gariaband district (proposed to move to Raipur district).

name: Kuleshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Rajim is an ancient pilgrimage town at the Triveni Sangam of the Mahanadi, Pairi and Sondur rivers, called the 'Prayag of Chhattisgarh'. Named after the Rajiv Lochan Mandir, it is officially in Gariaband district (proposed for Raipur district), about 45-50 km from Raipur, with a 2011 census population of about 14,090. The town hosts the annual Rajim Kumbh Mela and is regarded as the cultural capital of Chhattisgarh.

travel.railway: Nearest major railhead Raipur Junction, ~45-50 km (verify)
travel.road: Connected by road to Raipur (~45 km) and Mahasamund (~25 km); pedestrian bridge links Rajim to the temple island
